notes:
ACCESS: DIRECT HTTP FETCH (tier a), no Playwright/Chrome needed. robots.txt fetched at https://www.ikea.com/robots.txt: no anthropic-ai/ClaudeBot/Claude-Web/Claude-User/Claude-SearchBot directive anywhere, no blanket Disallow: / for User-agent: *; the sik.search.blue.cdtapps.com API host is not named either. Homepage https://www.ikea.com/in/en/ returned HTTP 200 via curl with a standard desktop User-Agent; no 403/CAPTCHA/DataDome/rate-limit at any point across ~95 HTTP requests (1 category page fetch + 91 product-count API calls). This mirrors the same IKEA global platform already vetted on UK/DE/FR/AE/JP (see f226.json Furniture notes), except this session used curl/urllib directly (tier a) rather than Claude-in-Chrome (tier c), since the site's own SSR HTML embeds the full category tree as inline JSON and the product-count API is reachable via plain HTTPS with a Referer header -- no browser rendering was required.

TREE METHOD: fetched https://www.ikea.com/in/en/cat/textiles-tl001/ (the Home Textiles department page) and extracted the embedded page-header <script type="text/hydrate"> JSON payload from the raw HTML, which contains data.config.catalogSlim -- an array of 23 top-level department nodes (ids st001, 700640, fu004, bm001, fu002, st007, ka001, kt001, tl001, de001, tl002, od001, ba001, li001, bc001, lc001, pp001, fb001, hi001, hs001, he001, pt001, wt001), each carrying a full recursive 'subs' child tree (830+ nodes site-wide, the same catalogSlim structure independently confirmed in this same session's Furniture f226.json). Walked catalogSlim for tl001 (Home textiles) and tl002 (Curtains & blinds) in full -- both are self-contained subtrees; tl002 is NOT nested under tl001 in India's own hierarchy, confirmed independently rather than assumed from another locale -- to build the Textile tree; walked st001 (Storage & organisation), st007 (Small storage & organisers), bm001 (Beds & mattresses, for 'Under bed storage'), lc001 (Laundry & cleaning), ba001 (Bathroom products), ka001 (Modular kitchens) and fu004 (Office furniture & gaming) for Storage-eligible nodes. India-specific check performed live: the plain URL /in/en/cat/textiles-tl002/ 301-redirects to /in/en/cat/curtains-blinds-tl002/ with canonical/h1 both reading 'Curtains & blinds', proving tl002 is its own India department distinct from tl001 'Home textiles'.

QTY METHOD: same sik.search.blue.cdtapps.com/in/en/product-list-page?category=<id> API used by this same session's Furniture extraction (f226.json), called directly via urllib with a desktop User-Agent and a Referer header (no browser needed -- the API has no CORS/session gate against a plain HTTPS client). qty = productListPage.productCount for every leaf; the API echoes back productListPage.category.name and .url for every id, and all 91 ids queried returned a category.name/url matching the expected id/slug exactly (no silent parent-listing substitution). plannerCount>0 triggers a +1 offset on the rendered listing header (a non-product planner-tool tile), the same behaviour already measured on IKEA UK/DE/FR/AE/JP and re-confirmed in this session's own Furniture pass (Sofas productCount=151, header '152 items'); qty recorded here is always the un-inflated productCount, never the header figure, and each row's evidence states both numbers.

GROUPING STRUCTURE: grouping-row labels and nesting follow India's own live catalogSlim hierarchy directly (Home textiles > Bedding > Bed linen / Duvets / Pillows; Cushions & cushion covers; Rugs; Children's textiles; Outdoor cushions; Table cloth and accessories; Bath towels and mats > Towels; Kitchen textiles; Baby textiles; Curtains & blinds > Curtains / Blinds), not a blind copy of another locale's group labels. Duplicate nodes that IKEA cross-lists under two parents in the same mega-menu (e.g. 'Cushions & cushion covers' appears both nested under Bedding and as its own top-level Home-textiles child; 'Children's bed linen'/'Children's duvets & pillows'/'Children's rugs'/'Baby towels & washcloths' each appear under both a room-specific parent and the cross-cutting 'Children's textiles'/'Baby textiles' parents) were recorded exactly once at their most specific canonical parent and skipped at the redundant parent, per the duplicate-prevention rule; the redundant parent was then dropped if it had no other surviving child (e.g. 'Baby textiles' keeps only 'Baby blankets & quilts' since its other four children -- baby bed linen, baby duvets & pillows, baby towels & washcloths, nursery rugs -- are recorded under Bedding/Bath towels/Rugs instead).

STORAGE-VS-FURNITURE BOUNDARY (the central judgment call on this company): India's 'Storage & organisation' (st001) top department is almost entirely modular/component FURNITURE -- Wardrobes, Chest of drawers & drawer units, Bookcases & shelving units, Display and Storage Cabinets, TV unit & media furniture, Sideboards & console tables, Shoe cabinets, Storage units & cabinets, Room dividers, Hallway furniture sets, and every named component system (PAX, BESTA, PLATSA, EKET, SMASTAD, IVAR, BROR, SKYTTA, JONAXEL, JOSTEIN, TROFAST, LASTARE, GULDDRAGARE, OMAR) -- and this SAME company's own Furniture extraction (pipeline/furniture_json_archive/f226.json) already explicitly claims essentially all of it as Furniture rows (Wardrobes, Chest of drawers, Bookshelves and Bookcases, Storage shelves & units, Cube shelves, Pantry, Basket drawer units, Shoe cabinets, Room dividers, Hallway furniture sets all appear verbatim in f226.json's Furniture rows) and explicitly documents excluding the whole named-system layer plus 'under-bed storage' as furniture parts/textiles. To avoid duplicate cross-category classification of the same nodes, this Storage pass did NOT re-claim anything already present in f226.json's Furniture rows (wardrobes/cabinets/bookcases/TV storage/sideboards/named systems), and did NOT re-claim 'Outdoor Storage' (21958, st001) since f226.json's Furniture notes explicitly flag it as an ambiguous furniture row already included there. Storage rows here instead come from the genuinely standalone, non-furniture storage-accessory departments/nodes: 'Small storage & organisers' (st007 -- boxes, baskets, organisers, bag organisers, food storage), 'Under bed storage' (bm001, explicitly excluded from Furniture's own list as furniture-parts/textile), 'Toy boxes & shelves' (the one non-named-system child surviving under st001's Children's storage & organisation branch, its TROFAST-system sibling excluded as a named component system), kitchen drawer/cupboard organisers and cutlery trays standalone under Modular kitchens (ka001), and Bathroom Storage/trolleys/laundry cabinets & shelving scattered under ba001/lc001.

EXCLUDED, and why: from Textile -- curtain hardware (curtain rods & rails, track systems, finials/brackets, explicit textile.md hardware exclusion); Venetian blinds and No-drill blinds (slat/mounting-type buckets, material not confirmed as fabric); Spa accessories (bath tools/brushes bundle, not confirmed textile); Sewing accessories (needles/thread/tools, not fabric). From Storage -- the entire Furniture-claimed layer described above; all named component systems; Wall shelves/floating shelves/complete wall shelves/picture ledges/brackets/plain 'Shelves'/Cube Storage (Wall Decor's job, same convention as this project's Furniture task); Hooks, Hangers, Hooks & hangers, Children's hooks & wall organisation (hardware, not storage); Noticeboards (office/decor, not storage); Recycling bins, Waste paper & pedal bins, Bin bags & liners, Bathroom bins (waste disposal, not storage of belongings -- not covered by any storage.md category); Cable management & accessories, Desk accessories, Moving supplies (mixed/generic accessory buckets, not a named storage category); Bathroom accessories subtree other than Bathroom organisers (shower accessories, soap dispensers, toilet brushes, toothbrush holders -- toiletry fixtures, storage.md Sec.14/28 exclusion); Bags department other than Bag organisers (shopping/tote/backpack/travel/cool bags -- fashion/carry items, storage.md Sec.6 exclusion); Water bottle & travel mugs, Cool bags (drinkware/travel accessories, Kitchen & Dining territory); Food storage accessories & resealable bags (disposable consumable, not a durable storage product); Kitchen shelves, Kitchen Rack & Wall storage's shelf child (Wall Decor's job, same convention applied to 'Kitchen shelves' as to the generic Wall shelves subtree); Laundry accessories (too generic/mixed to confirm storage-only contents), Drying racks, Ironing boards (laundry tools/appliances, not storage containers); all METOD/ENHET kitchen-cabinet-system parts, doors, fronts, worktops (fitted-kitchen furniture components, not general-retail storage); Storage units & cabinets (home and office) and Trolleys/fu005 (cabinet- and cart-furniture, consistent with the Furniture boundary already drawn on this company).

SANITY CHECKS: all 91 queried category ids returned productListPage.category.name/url exactly matching the expected id/slug (zero silent parent-listing substitutions); qty values span 1-106 across the 95 leaves with 50+ distinct values, no site-wide constant or suspiciously round cap; low counts (e.g. Children's duvets & pillows=1, Fur rugs=2, Anti-slip & underlays=2, Bag organisers=3) match the general small-niche-category pattern already documented on this same India storefront in f226.json and are treated as genuine, not errors. MANUAL REVIEW flags (14 rows, all MEDIUM confidence) mark nodes where IKEA bundles a textile/storage item with an adjacent non-textile/non-storage item under one shared URL with no further sub-split available, or where the rule files do not explicitly enumerate the exact product type (e.g. filled 'Pillows' as distinct from pillowcases/pillow covers) -- each flag states the specific ambiguity inline in that row's flag field.
